defects.currentClaim: The entire sugya is framed as a dispute over 'wine storehouses': Rav Kahana holds storehouses for hay/cattle are exempt but wood/wine are obligated because women enter them 'to draw wine'; Rav Yehuda holds wood is exempt but wine is obligated; the interpretive crux is whether 'nashim ne'otot bahen' means women draw wine (domestic, Rav Kahana) or women bring wine to sell there (commercial, Rav Yehuda). The Gemara is said to cite two baraitot about which storehouses are obligated, resolved on 11b.
defects.sourceSupport: The Hebrew source and Rashi state the opposite framing entirely. Rav Kahana teaches before Rav Yehuda that bet ha-teven, bet ha-baqar, bet ha-etzim, and bet ha-otzarot (hay-house, cattle-house, wood-house, general storehouse) are ALL exempt (not split hay/cattle-exempt vs wood/wine-obligated) because 'ha-nashim na'ot bahen'. The dispute over the meaning of na'ot is bathing (rochatzot, Rashi confirms explicitly: 'mai na'ot? rochatzot' -- because it is a place of disgrace, women stand there naked, unfit for the honor of Heaven to have a mezuza there) versus adorning themselves (mitkashtot, with perfumes, per Rashi). There is no wine in this dispute at all, and no concept of women 'drawing wine' or 'bringing wine to sell'. Two conflicting baraitot are cited: one that excludes the four listed houses from mezuza (with a dissenting 'v'yesh mechayvin'), and a second ('be'emet ameru') that separately exempts the bathroom-house (beit ha-kise), tannery-house (beit ha-bursaki), bathhouse (beit ha-merchatz), and immersion-house (beit ha-tevila) where women na'ot. Rav Kahana and Rav Yehuda each reconcile this baraita pair per their own reading of na'ot (bathing vs. adorning). Wine/oil storehouses appear exactly once, at vilnaLine 49-50, as part of the opening of an entirely separate baraita ('u-vi-she'arecha... rafet ve-lulin u-matben ve-otzarot yayin ve-otzarot shemen chayavin be-mezuza') that plainly obligates them in mezuza with no dispute -- this is not part of the na'ot controversy and is only reached in the daf's closing, unfinished lines.
defects.requiredCorrection: Rewrite display, learning, argumentFlow, topicTags, misconceptions, visualizableElements, quizSeeds, and prerequisiteKnowledge to reflect the actual dispute: Rav Kahana taught before Rav Yehuda that the hay-house/cattle-house/wood-house/storehouse are exempt from mezuza because women na'ot there; the interpretive fight is whether na'ot means bathing (Rav Kahana, per Rashi: a place of nakedness/disgrace unfit for a mezuza) or adorning themselves (an alternate reading tested and contradicted by a second baraita about a cattle-pen where adorning women DO obligate mezuza, forcing 'mitkashtot' to be recognized as itself a tannaitic dispute). A separate, structurally parallel baraita pair addresses the bathroom-house/tannery-house/bathhouse/immersion-house as independently exempt where women na'ot, which Rav Kahana and Rav Yehuda each reconcile according to their own na'ot reading (including whether the bathhouse clause must separately teach public vs. private bathhouse). The daf ends mid-word inside the opening of a new, unrelated 'bi-she'arecha' gates baraita (which does plainly obligate wine- and oil-storehouses, without dispute) -- unresolved, continuing on 11b. finalRuling should remain null (per the daf's own incompleteness); difficulty/alternateAngles/relatedSugyot/conceptRefs/requiresUnderstanding may be retained if not wine-specific, but must be checked and rewritten wherever they presuppose the fabricated wine-storehouse narrative.

reconstructedStructure: Lines 1-6: baraita that all Temple gates lacked mezuza except Nicanor Gate; Gemara asks whose tanna this reflects, resolves gezeira-ligzeira concern by treating gate+Parhedrin chamber as one combined decree. Line 6 is a split line: ends this sugya ('כולה חדא גזירה היא') and opens the next baraita ('ת"ר בשעריך') in the same line.

Lines 6-25: baraita on 'bisha'arecha' (house/courtyard/province/town gates) obligating mezuza; Rav Safra/Abaye exchange on Machoza's gateless walls; danger rationale (public mezuzot checked twice per jubilee); Rav Yehuda's account of Artavan checking mezuzot in Tzippori's upper market and being charged 1000 zuz by a kasdor; challenge from R. Elazar's shluchei-mitzva-protection principle; resolved via kavua sakana, proven from Samuel's fear of Saul when told to anoint David (1 Samuel 16:2) as an unrelated scriptural proof text.

Lines 26-51: Rav Kahana teaches before Rav Yehuda that hay/cattle/wood/storehouse are exempt because 'nashim ne'otot bahen'; dispute over meaning (bathe vs. adorn) each refuted by a baraita; Rav Kahana concludes both questions are tannaitic disputes; further baraita on bathroom/tannery/bathhouse/mikveh, each amora reconciling per his own view; final baraita on 'bisha'arecha' seemingly obligating barn/coops/storehouses; daf cuts off mid-word at 'בית' (line 51), continuing on 11b.

reviewEvidence.independentSourceReconstruction: Read raw Hebrew vilnaLine 26-51 of 11a.json before viewing candidate enrichment. Line 26 tail ('לזבוח לה' באתי') is the end of the prior sugya; the current sugya opens with 'תני רב כהנא קמיה דרב יהודה' (26-27): Rav Kahana teaches before Rav Yehuda that hay-, cattle-, wood-, and general storehouses are exempt from mezuza because women 'ne'otot' (use) them, glossed as bathing (rochatzot). Rav Yehuda challenges (29-31): if the reason is bathing, an unmarked storehouse should be obligated -- yet a baraita exempts a cattle barn unconditionally. The Gemara reinterprets ne'otot as 'adorn themselves' (32-33), but Rav Kahana counters (33-35) that another baraita obligates a barn where women adorn themselves, refuting that reading too. The Gemara concludes (36-38) both the meaning of ne'otot and the status of an unmarked storehouse are themselves tannaitic disputes, supported by a baraita on 'beitcha beitcha hamyuchad lecha.' A further baraita (38-40) states bathroom/tannery/bathhouse/mikveh are always exempt ('be'emet amru'), and each amora reconciles it with his own view ('matretz le-ta'ame'). Rav Kahana's reconciliation runs 41-45a: storehouses exempt in the unmarked case (with a dissenting view obligating it); the be'emet-amru group exempt because na'ot=bathe there; the Gemara then asks why bathhouse is listed twice and answers this teaches BOTH a public and a private bathhouse are exempt, since one might think a private bathhouse (less filth, 'lo nafish zuhama') should be obligated -- this public/private-bathhouse clarification and its 'nafish zuhama' reasoning belong entirely to Rav Kahana's reconciliation, ending at 'קמ"ל' mid-line-45. Only then, at the tail of line 45 ('ורב יהודה מתרץ לטעמיה הכי קתני'), does Rav Yehuda's own reconciliation begin, running 45b-48: storehouses exempt even where women adorn themselves (with a dissent obligating the adorning case), but everyone agrees the unmarked case is exempt; the be'emet-amru group is exempt even though women adorn themselves there, because their filth is extensive ('mishum denafish zuhama') -- Rav Yehuda's text contains no public-vs-private-bathhouse distinction at all. Lines 48-51 raise a further baraita on 'bisha'arecha' obligating gate-houses, courtyards, cities, towns, a barn, coops, hay- and wine/oil-storehouses in mezuza, challenging Rav Yehuda; the daf physically ends mid-word ('בית', line 51) before any resolution, which continues on 11b.

No 11b-resolution leak was found anywhere in display, learning, argumentFlow, misconceptions, quizSeeds, visualizableElements, topicTags, or prerequisiteKnowledge -- the prior audited leak defect is not present in this candidate.

defects.claim: The candidate attributes the public-vs-private-bathhouse distinction ('the bathroom group is exempt because their filth is extensive, distinguishing a public bathhouse from a private one') to Rav Yehuda's reconciliation, citing vilnaLine 45 for 'Rav Yehuda's reconciliation, including the public-vs-private bathhouse distinction.'
defects.sourceShows: Vilna lines 44-45 ('אי הכי היינו מרחץ אשמעינן מרחץ דרבים ואשמעינן מרחץ דיחיד דס"ד אמינא מרחץ דרבים דנפיש זוהמיה אבל מרחץ דיחיד דלא נפיש זוהמיה אימא ליחייב במזוזה קמ"ל') falls entirely inside Rav Kahana's reconciliation, which opens at the start of line 41 ('רב כהנא מתרץ לטעמיה') and does not end until 'קמ"ל' partway through line 45. Rav Yehuda's reconciliation only begins at the words immediately following, at the tail of line 45 ('ורב יהודה מתרץ לטעמיה הכי קתני'), and his actual reasoning for the bathroom/tannery/bathhouse/mikveh group (line 48, 'משום דנפיש זוהמיה') never distinguishes a public from a private bathhouse -- that distinction is Rav Kahana's alone.
defects.requiredCorrection: Move the public-vs-private-bathhouse clarification and its 'nafish zuhama' reasoning into Rav Kahana's reconciliation (step-05's Rav Kahana clause, sourced to vilnaLine 41/44-45a), and restate Rav Yehuda's clause (sourced to the tail of vilnaLine 45 through 48) as: storehouses exempt even where women adorn themselves, with a dissent obligating the adorning case, but everyone agrees the unmarked case is exempt; the bathroom/tannery/bathhouse/mikveh group is exempt because their filth is extensive -- with no public/private split in Rav Yehuda's version.

independentSourceReconstruction.text: Rav Kahana's baraita exempts hay, cattle, wood and storehouses because women ne'otot there; bathing is challenged by an unconditional cattle-barn exemption, adorning is challenged by an adorning-barn obligation, and Rav Kahana concludes both questions are tannaitic disputes. The further baraita exempts bathroom, tannery, bathhouse, mikveh and places women use. Rav Kahana reads the dispute as plain-case and ne'otot=bathing; Rav Yehuda reads it as adorning-case with plain cases universally exempt, and explains the listed places by filth. The final baraita appears to obligate gates, barn, coop, hay, wine and oil storehouses; the daf ends at בית and resolution continues on 11b.

# Yoma 12a — First-pass source-first audit evidence

Review id: yoma-12a-firstpass-20261002

## sugya yoma-012a-s01 (lines 1-30) — REPAIR_REQUIRED

Raw text (vilnaLine 11-19):
"מה היה בחלקו של יהודה הר הבית הלשכות והעזרות ומה היה בחלקו של בנימין אולם
והיכל ובית קדשי הקדשים ורצועה היתה יוצאה מחלקו של יהודה ונכנסת לחלקו של
בנימין ובה היה מזבח בנוי ובנימין הצדיק היה מצטער עליה לבלעה בכל יום שנאמר
חופף עליו כל היום לפיכך זכה בנימין הצדיק ונעשה אושפיזכן לגבורה שנאמר ובין
כתפיו שכן"

evidence.independentSourceFlowReconstruction: Lines 1-3 continue a 12a answer: 'avodato m'chanakhto' - the replacement Kohen Gadol (KG) is inaugurated into office by his own performance of Yom Kippur service, proven from the rule that Moshe's Mishkan vessels alone required anointing for consecration, while every vessel made thereafter was consecrated by use alone. Lines 4-19 open a dispute about the belt (avnet) of the ordinary priest (kohen hedyot): is it kilayim (wool-linen, like the KG's regular-year belt) or pure linen/buz (like the KG's Yom Kippur belt)? Rav Dimi transmits a dispute between Rabbi and R. Elazar b'R. Shimon without specifying positions; the Gemara tries (lines 7-13) to prove from a baraita ('the only difference between KG and hedyot is the belt') that Rabbi holds kilayim, concluding the baraita must be limited to Yom Kippur equivalences. Lines 13-19: Ravin then transmits the dispute with positions attached - unanimous that the KG's own belt is linen on Yom Kippur and kilayim the rest of the year; the live dispute is only about the hedyot's belt (Rabbi: kilayim; R. Elazar b'R. Shimon: linen). Lines 19-29: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak cites a baraita on 'al besaro yilbash' (Lev. 6): R. Yehuda reads it to include mitznefet+avnet for the ash-removal (terumat hadeshen) service; R. Dosa reads it to teach that the KG's Yom Kippur garments become usable afterward by an ordinary priest. Rabbi gives two rebuttals of R. Dosa (the YK avnet is linen, not the same garment as the hedyot's kilayim avnet, so it cannot be reused as such; and in any case a garment used for greater sanctity may not be reused for lesser sanctity) and reads 'yilbash' instead as including even threadbare/worn garments in the obligation. Lines 29-31 (spanning the s02/s03 boundary): the Gemara notes R. Dosa is consistent with his own view elsewhere, that 'and he shall leave them there' (Lev. 16) teaches the Yom Kippur garments require genizah (storage) - R. Dosa holds he may not reuse them even on a later Yom Kippur. Lines 31-41: a baraita (Tana D'vei Rav): if a disqualification befalls the KG and a second kohen is appointed in his place, then when the first returns to service, R. Meir holds the second remains fully bound by all the personal obligations of the High Priesthood; R. Yosei holds the second is fit for neither the High Priesthood (the first is restored) nor the ordinary priesthood (one may not demote from a higher sanctity, 'ma'alin bakodesh ve'lo moridin'). R. Yosei supports this with the real case of Yosef ben Ilim of Tzippori, so ruled by the Sages, explicitly for the two reasons of rivalry (eivah) and non-demotion. Lines 41-42: Rabba bar bar Chana cites R. Yochanan beginning a halachic ruling - 'halacha...' - and the daf physically ends here, mid-word/mid-sentence, with the content of the ruling (which position is accepted, and on which dispute) not stated anywhere on 12b. It continues onto 13a.

entries.note: Text: 'מלמד שטעונין גניזה רבי דוסא אומר שלא' (continuation of R. Dosa's genizah teaching begun at line 29). Falls between s02's declaredLineRange end (29) and s03's declaredLineRange start (31). No sugya claims this line; it is also entirely absent in substance from both sugyot's enrichment fields.

Line 31 itself is a split line: its first clause ('ישתמש בהן יוה"כ אחר') is the tail of R. Dosa's genizah teaching (thematically s02 content), and only the second clause ('ת"ר אירע בו פסול') begins s03's actual topic. s03's declaredLineRange silently absorbs the tail of a different topic because Vilna lines are the finest granularity available; this does not excuse line 30's total omission.

Daf physically ends mid-word within 'הלכה' (Rabba bar bar Chana citing R. Yochanan beginning a halachic ruling). dafEndState = MID_ARGUMENT/OTHER_OPEN_CONTINUATION: the content and subject of this ruling are not recoverable from 12b and continue on 13a.

physicalLineCoverageLedger.summary: 41 of 42 physical Vilna lines are claimed by a declared sugya range (s01: 1-3, s02: 4-29, s03: 31-42). Line 30 is an orphan: owned by no sugya, and its content (R. Dosa's genizah teaching) is also substantively absent from both neighboring sugyot's enrichment. This is a physical coverage gap, not merely a cosmetic boundary issue.

dafBoundaryVerdict.note: The daf ends mid-citation: 'amar Rabba bar bar Chana amar R. Any claim on 12b asserting a specific halachic conclusion tied to this line is importing unstated 13a content.

dafSummaryFindings.issue: Minor completeness gap, not a factual error: the daf-level summary describes the belt dispute (lines 4-19) and the two-KGs dispute (lines 31-41) but omits any mention of the R. Dosa/Rabbi exchange over reusing Yom Kippur garments and the genizah requirement (lines 19-31), which is a distinct substantive topic on the page and is also the location of the orphaned line 30.
dafSummaryFindings.correction: Add a clause noting the baraita on 'al besaro yilbash', R. Dosa's view that Yom Kippur garments may be reused by an ordinary priest, Rabbi's rejection of that view, and R. Dosa's own genizah teaching, before the summary moves to the two-KGs dispute.

sugyaVerdicts.boundaryNote: Lines 1-3 form a complete, self-contained unit (the 'avodato m'chanakhto' answer and its Temple-vessel proof) before the belt dispute opens cleanly at line 4. No overlap, no gap, no misowned content.

findings.issue: lineId 'yoma-12b-l01' is missing the zero-padding used everywhere else on this daf ('yoma-012b-l01', as used in argumentFlow[0].sourceRefs[0]). Coordinate inconsistency, not a content error.
findings.correction: Normalize to 'yoma-012b-l01' to match the id scheme used by the other sourceRefs on this daf.

sugyaVerdicts.cleanFieldsStatement: Every field listed above was individually checked against lines 1-3 and the Rashi on those lines. The 'avodato m'chanakhto' attribution, the Temple-vessel analogy, the claim that no formal initiation ceremony is required, and the relatedSugyot pointers back to 12a are all accurately and fully supported by the authoritative text.

sugyaVerdicts.boundaryNote: The declared range (4-29) is correct at its start but its end silently truncates the R. Dosa/genizah unit it opens at line 29, leaving line 30 (the direct continuation of that same sentence) orphaned rather than included. The range should extend to cover the full unit it begins.

findings.currentClaim: "Halacha: the common priest's belt is kilayim (following Rabbi's position as clarified by Ravin)."
findings.sourceSupport: No line in 4-29 (or anywhere on 12b) states a halachic ruling on the hedyot's belt. The only halacha-introducing sentence on the entire daf is line 41-42 ('amar Rabba bar bar Chana amar R. Yochanan halacha...'), which is physically cut off mid-word, sits inside s03's range (31-42), and is contextually attached to the immediately preceding R. Meir/R. Yosei dispute, not to the belt dispute 12+ lines earlier.
findings.whatSourceActuallySupports: The daf only reports that Rabbi holds kilayim and R. Elazar b'Rabbi Shimon holds linen for the hedyot's belt (per Ravin, lines 13-19), with no resolution stated on 12b.
findings.correction: Remove the asserted halachic conclusion. State that the dispute between Rabbi and R. Elazar b'Rabbi Shimon over the hedyot's belt is left open on 12b; if a resolution is wanted, it must be sourced to wherever (13a or later) the Gemara's halachic literature actually states it, with crossReference set true and a real supporting line range on that daf.

findings.currentClaim: "Halacha follows Rabbi: the common priest's belt is kilayim all year and does not change to match the KG's Yom Kippur linen."
findings.sourceSupport: Same defect as finalRuling above - no halachic resolution appears in lines 4-29.
findings.correction: Rephrase as a description of the live dispute (Rabbi: kilayim; R. Elazar b'Rabbi Shimon: linen) rather than a resolved halacha.

findings.issue: Lines 19-29 contain a second, distinct sub-topic (R. Dosa's reading of 'al besaro yilbash' as permitting reuse of the KG's Yom Kippur garments by an ordinary priest; Rabbi's two-part rebuttal; the 'yilbash' includes-worn-garments conclusion; and R. Dosa's own consistency teaching on genizah) that is entirely unrepresented in display, learning, argumentFlow, misconceptions, and quizSeeds. The existing argumentFlow step-04 (vilnaLine 26) only describes R. Yehuda's mitznefet/avnet-for-ash-removal reading and mischaracterizes it as 'showing this supports Rabbi's kilayim position' - a connection the text does not state; R. Yehuda's statement is not framed in the Gemara as support for Rabbi over R. Elazar b'Rabbi Shimon.
findings.correction: Add an argumentFlow step (or steps) covering R. Dosa's view, Rabbi's two rebuttals, and the 'yilbash includes worn garments' conclusion, each correctly attributed and sourced to lines 21-28; correct or remove the unsupported 'showing this supports Rabbi's kilayim position' framing in the existing step-04; extend declaredLineRange/content ownership through line 30 to close the orphan-line gap identified in the coverage ledger.

findings.issue: lineId is 'yoma-12b-l08' (no such id pattern matches vilna line 22 elsewhere on this daf; argumentFlow step-03 uses 'yoma-012b-l22' for the same vilna line 22). The lineId and vilnaLine in this sourceRef do not correspond to each other under the daf's own id convention.
findings.correction: Normalize to 'yoma-012b-l22' to match vilnaLine 22 and the id scheme used by argumentFlow step-03.

sugyaVerdicts.boundaryNote: Start at line 31 is defensible as the point the new baraita's main clause begins, notwithstanding that line 31's first few words are the tail of the preceding R. Dosa/genizah unit (see coverage ledger note on line 31). End at line 42 correctly reaches the physical end of the daf.

findings.currentClaim: "Halacha follows R. Yosei: the replacement KG is suspended from both offices while the original lives, as in the case of Yosef ben Elem."
findings.sourceSupport: Line 41-42 ('amar Rabba bar bar Chana amar R. Yochanan halacha...') is the only halacha-introducing clause on the daf, and it is physically cut off mid-word. 12b itself never states which side (R. Meir or R. Yosei) the halacha follows; that content, if it exists at all in the Gemara's continuation, is on 13a.
findings.whatSourceActuallySupports: The daf supports only that R. Meir and R. Yosei disagree (lines 31-35), and that R. Yosei's position was applied in practice to Yosef ben Ilim of Tzippori by the Sages (lines 35-41) - i.e. a reported historical ruling in that one case, not a generalized Amoraic halachic statement that 12b itself completes.
findings.correction: Remove the assertion that 'halacha follows R. Yosei' as a conclusion reached on 12b. It is legitimate to note that the Yosef ben Ilim incident shows the Sages ruled like R. Yosei in that historical case; it is not legitimate to present Rabba bar bar Chana's cut-off 'halacha' citation as confirming this generally, since 12b never discloses what that citation concludes. If the intended target daf's content (13a) genuinely states 'halacha k'R. Yosei', that claim belongs on 13a's own record, sourced to 13a's lines, not retrofitted onto 12b.

findings.currentClaim: "Halacha follows R. Yosei: the replacement KG is suspended from both offices while the original lives, as the case of Yosef ben Elem of Tzippori shows."
findings.correction: Rephrase as: the Yosef ben Ilim case shows the Sages ruled in practice like R. Yosei's reasoning (suspended from both offices, for the stated reasons of rivalry and non-demotion); do not claim this as the daf's own stated halachic conclusion of the R. Meir/R. Yosei dispute.

findings.issue: step-03 ('Yosef ben Elem: serves in an emergency but otherwise excluded') and the attached quizSeed cite vilnaLine 42 as support for an 'emergency exception' claim. Line 42 contains only the single word 'הלכה' - it supports nothing about an emergency exception. This appears to be enrichment carried from elsewhere (likely genuinely belongs to the Mishnah/Gemara passage on 13a about an emergency substitute) misattributed to line 42 of 12b.
findings.whatSourceActuallySupports: Line 42 supports nothing beyond the bare word 'halacha' beginning a citation that is cut off.
findings.correction: Remove step-03 and its quizSeed, or re-source them properly to 13a with crossReference set true if that is where the emergency-service exception is actually stated; do not leave vilnaLine 42 on 12b as the cited support for a claim 12b's text does not contain.

sugyaVerdicts.allSugyotImpact: SHARED_DAF_DATA_NOT_IMPLICATED: s03's defects (unsupported halachic conclusions, a misattributed line-42 citation) are local to s03's own fields and do not require retargeting sibling sugyot, independent of the separate line-30 boundary issue that does require --all-sugyot.

evidence.methodology: Read authoritativeHebrewLines 1-42 start to finish before inspecting candidate enrichment. Independently reconstructed topic flow and sugya boundaries, then audited each declared field against source. First-pass evidence and certification registry content were not consulted.

independentSourceReconstruction.lines1to3: Continuation of 12a: 'his service inducts him' - proof from Temple vessels (Moshe's vessels anointed; from then on, consecration by use/service alone, per the Shevuot 15a derivation of 'them').
independentSourceReconstruction.lines4to19: Dispute over the common (ordinary) priest's belt material (kilayim vs. linen/buz), transmitted two ways: Rav Dimi names the disputants (Rabbi, R. Elazar b'R. Shimon) without positions; the Gemara's own analysis tries both assignments and rejects the 'rest of year' reading via redundancy; Ravin's tradition assigns Rabbi=kilayim, R. Elazar b'R. Shimon=linen explicitly.
independentSourceReconstruction.lines19to28: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak cites a mishna/baraita on 'al besaro yilbash' (Lev. 6, ash-removal passage): R. Yehuda reads it to include mitznefet+avnet in that service; R. Dosa reads it to include the KG's Yom Kippur garments becoming usable afterward by an ordinary priest; Rabbi gives two rebuttals (YK avnet is linen, not the hedyot's kilayim avnet; and greater-sanctity garments cannot be downgraded to lesser-sanctity use) and instead reads 'yilbash' to include worn-out garments.
independentSourceReconstruction.lines29to31a: The Gemara notes R. Dosa is self-consistent: a baraita on 'and he shall leave them there' (Lev. 16) teaches the YK garments require genizah; R. Dosa holds this means not even the KG may reuse them on a later Yom Kippur (clause completes on line 31 before the new topic begins).
independentSourceReconstruction.lines31bto42: New topic (ת"ר): a disqualification befalls the KG and a replacement is appointed; when the original recovers and returns to service, dispute over the replacement's status - R. Meir: still bound by full KG obligations; R. Yosei: unfit for either KG or ordinary-priest service. R. Yosei illustrated via the historical case of Yosef ben Elem of Tzippori, with the Sages ruling as R. Yosei for the stated reasons (KG: rivalry/eivah; ordinary priest: we elevate but do not demote in sanctity). Daf ends mid-word on a halacha-introducing clause (Rabba bar bar Chana citing R. Yochanan), carrying over to 13a.

boundaryLeakageSweep.line31SplitFinding: Vilna line 31 straddles two topics: the tail clause of R. Dosa's genizah-consistency ruling (continuing the s02 topic from lines 29-30) and the opening of the new ת"ר baraita about a disqualified KG and his replacement (the s03 topic, and the majority of the line's content). The declared boundary (s02 ends 30 / s03 begins 31) assigns the physical line to the sugya whose topic dominates it (s03), consistent with the lineMap/sefariaRef convention elsewhere on this daf where a vilnaLine is assigned to the sugya of its first new sefariaRef. sugyaReviews.findings: Rav Pappa's ruling (service itself inducts the replacement KG) and the Temple-vessel proof (Moshe's vessels anointed; thereafter consecration by use, per Shevuot 15a) are accurately and completely represented. Speaker attribution, proof structure, and the vessel analogy all match lines 1-3 and the supporting Rashi (vilnaLine 1-4 Rashi commentary). No field misstates source content, chronology, or attribution. Boundary (1-3) is a coherent, self-contained unit continuing the 12a question with no leakage into line 4's belt topic.

All seven argumentFlow steps match source order and content: (1) belt question framed, (2) Rav Dimi's unattributed dispute (line 6), (3) Ravin's attributed positions (line 13/19 region - Rabbi=kilayim, R. Elazar b'R. Shimon=linen), (4) baraita on 'al besaro yilbash' with R. Yehuda's reading (line 19-21), (5) R. Dosa's reading re: reuse of KG's YK garments (line 22-23), (6) Rabbi's two rebuttals and his own 'worn garments' reading (lines 24-28), (7) R. Dosa's self-consistent genizah teaching (lines 29-30, correctly narrated through its line-31 completion). Speaker names, ruling content, and the two distinct rebuttal reasons (identity of the avnet; no downgrading from greater to lesser sanctity) are all accurate. misconceptions correctly isolate that the dispute is limited to the belt (not all four garments) and that R. Dosa's reading is rejected twice over (by Rabbi, and by R. Dosa's own genizah position). No field attributes content from s01 or s03 into this range, and no required field is missing or reversed.

Core dispute (R. Meir: replacement retains full KG obligations; R. Yosei: replacement unfit for either office) and the Yosef ben Elem of Tzippori illustration, plus the two stated reasons (KG: rivalry/eivah; hedyot: ma'alin bakodesh velo moridin), all match lines 31-41 accurately. finalRuling is appropriately cautious that 12b itself does not resolve R. Meir vs. R. Yosei and correctly flags that line 42 ('halacha') is a physical cutoff carrying over to 13a - this matches the source exactly. However, quizSeeds[0].sourceRefs[0].lineId is set to "yoma-12b-l11", which is both malformed relative to this daf's lineId convention used throughout the packet (should be zero-padded "012b") and encodes the wrong line number: the question/answer concerns vilnaLine 31 (also stated in the same object's own vilnaLine field), and every other sourceRef for this content elsewhere in the sugya correctly uses "yoma-012b-l31" (see argumentFlow step-01 sourceRefs). "yoma-12b-l11" instead points to line 11, which is mid-belt-dispute content from s02, not this sugya's topic - a cross-sugya misattribution in a citation field.

evidence.methodology: Read authoritativeHebrewLines (all 42 Vilna lines) start to finish before reading any enrichment. Independently reconstructed the daf's flow: (1) lines 1-3, Rav Pappa's answer that the replacement KG's first act of service itself initiates him (s01, already second-passed, inspected only for boundary/shared-payload validation); (2) lines 4-19, the common priest's belt (kilayim vs buz) dispute, reported ambiguously by Rav Dimi (lines 4-13, with an attempted proof via a baraita on 'ein bein KG l'hedyot ela avnet') then resolved unambiguously by Ravin (lines 13-19: Rabbi=kilayim, R. Elazar b'R. Shimon=linen for the hedyot; both agree KG is linen on YK, kilayim rest of year); (3) lines 19-30, a separate baraita on 'al besaro yilbash' (Lev. 6, terumat hadeshen context): R. Yehuda reads it to include mitznefet/avnet in the ash-removal obligation, R. Dosa reads it to mean the KG's used YK garments become valid for an ordinary priest; Rabbi rebuts R. Dosa with two answers (the YK avnet and hedyot avnet are not the same garment; greater-sanctity garments may not be downgraded to lesser-sanctity use) and instead reads 'yilbash' to include worn-out garments; the Gemara then notes R. Dosa is self-consistent via a second baraita ('v'hinicham sham' = genizah required, so R. Dosa holds the YK garments may never be reused, not even on a later YK) - this ruling's completing clause physically falls on line 31 due to Sefaria/Vilna segment 10/11 splitting the sentence mid-clause; (4) lines 31-42, a new baraita: if the KG was disqualified and replaced, then recovers, what is the replacement's status - R. Meir (retains all KG obligations) vs R. Yosei (suspended from both offices); the Yosef ben Elem of Tzippori case shows the Sages ruled practically like R. Yosei (for eivah/maalin b'kodesh reasons); daf ends mid-sentence on the bare word 'halacha' (Rabba bar bar Chana citing R. Yochanan), resolved only on 13a ('halacha k'Rabbi Yosei') - a genuine open 12b->13a boundary. Declared sugya ranges (s01: 1-3, s02: 4-30, s03: 31-42) are contiguous and non-overlapping across all 42 lines - no gap, no duplication at the sugya-range level.

targets.reasoning: Two linked SEMANTIC fields misattribute which source resolves the belt-identity dispute, conflating two independent sugya threads into one false causal chain. display.hint states: 'The baraita from Leviticus 6 resolves the identity question: Rabbi endorses kilayim for the common priest, making him parallel to the KG on regular days.' learning.coreMove states the baraita 'independently corroborates Rabbi's position by showing the avnet is one of the four mandatory garments in that same verse.' Both claims are false on the source: the identity question (whether Rabbi holds kilayim or linen for the hedyot's belt) is fully and explicitly resolved earlier, by Ravin's report alone (lines 13-19: 'lo nechleku ela b'avneto shel kohen hedyot... sh'Rabbi omer shel kilayim v'Rabbi Elazar b'Rabbi Shimon omer shel butz'), with no ambiguity left open at that point. The baraita on 'al besaro yilbash' (lines 19-30, introduced by Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak) is a textually and topically separate inquiry - whether the mitznefet/avnet are obligated for terumat hadeshen (R. Yehuda), or whether the KG's worn YK garments become usable by an ordinary priest (R. Dosa) - unrelated to proving who holds which material. Rabbi's rebuttal of R. Dosa (lines 24-28) merely presupposes his own already-settled position (that the hedyot's avnet differs in material from the KG's YK avnet) as a premise to distinguish the two garments; it is not a new proof text that 'resolves' or 'corroborates' the identity dispute, and it says nothing about the avnet being 'one of the four mandatory garments in that same verse' as a corroborating mechanism for the kilayim/linen question. The candidate's framing therefore invents a resolving/corroborating relationship between two sugya segments that does not exist in the source, misstating the daf's actual logical structure (a 'reasons'/'logic' defect, not merely a stylistic one). This requires a text fix to display.hint and learning.coreMove (and any dependent summary/learnerQuestion phrasing that relies on the same false linkage) rather than acceptance as-is.
targets.secondaryObservation: Minor, non-blocking: argumentFlow step-07's claim that R. Dosa 'holds he may not reuse them even on a later Yom Kippur' textually completes only on physical line 31 (Sefaria Yoma.12b.10/12b.11 split the clause 'she'lo yishtamesh bahen Yom Kippur acher' across the segment/line boundary), which is one line past s02's declared endVilnaLine of 30. This is an unavoidable artifact of vilna-line-granularity segmentation on a source sentence that itself straddles the 12b.10/12b.11 Sefaria boundary (the new baraita 'Tanu Rabbanan' that opens s03 begins later within that same line 31). The asserted content is accurate and does not duplicate or omit anything in s03; it is noted for completeness per the exhaustive physical-coverage sweep but is not independently sufficient to reject this target.

Step-01 (l04) and step-02 (l06) both draw on content split across the physical line 5/6 boundary ('chad amar shel [line break] kilayim'); legitimate given lineId segments span multiple Vilna lines as documented. Step-03 (l13) matches Ravin's clarification at lines 13-19. Step-04 (l19) matches the baraita's opening/R. Yehuda reading at lines 19-21. Step-05 (l22) matches R. Dosa's reading at lines 22-23. Step-06 cites lineId l22/vilnaLine 24 for Rabbi's rebuttal (lines 24-28); the lineId points to the segment containing the start of that content, consistent with segment granularity. targets.reasoning: Independently re-derived from lines 31-42: a baraita on a KG disqualified and replaced, then recovering; R. Meir holds the replacement retains full KG personal obligations (line 33, 'kol mitzvot kehuna gedola alav'), R. Yosei holds the replacement is suspended from both KG and ordinary-priest status (lines 34-35, 'eino ra'ui lo l'kohen gadol v'lo l'kohen hedyot'). The candidate's display/learning fields accurately state both positions and correctly frame the tension as a collision between 'cannot serve (original is alive)' and 'cannot be demoted (ein moridin)'. The Yosef ben Elem of Tzippori narrative (lines 35-41) is correctly attributed: the candidate correctly distinguishes that the practical ruling in that story is stated in the name of 'chachamim' (the Sages, lines 37-40) reaching R. Yosei's result (suspended from both, for eivah/maalin bakodesh), without overclaiming that the daf itself formally adopts R. Yosei's view over R. Meir's - this nuance is explicitly and correctly preserved in finalRuling. finalRuling also correctly identifies that the daf's halacha-clause (Rabba bar bar Chana citing R. Yochanan, line 41-42) is cut off after the bare word 'halacha' and that the resolution ('halacha k'Rabbi Yosei') is a known fact of 13a's continuation, not stated on 12b itself - this is the correct, source-grounded handling of the 12b->13a open-boundary risk the review was asked to scrutinize, properly distinguished from being presented as 12b's own conclusion. No misattributed speakers, quantities, chronology, or proof texts found. No sourceRef draws on lines outside 31-42 without appropriate framing as a forward (13a) reference, and that single forward reference is correctly hedged as 'cut off mid-sentence' rather than asserted as this daf's content.

reviewEvidence.independentSourceReconstruction: Vilna 13a lines 1-5: 'halacha k'R. Yosei umodeh R. Yosei she'im avar ve'avad avodato kesherah. Amar Rav Yehuda amar Rav: halacha k'R. Yosei umodeh R. Yosei she'im met rishon shechozer la'avodato. Pshita! Mahu detimah hoveya lei tzarah mechayim, kama lan.' Translation: Halacha follows R. Yosei, and R. Yosei concedes that if [the suspended replacement] transgressed and performed the service, it is valid. Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: halacha follows R. Yosei, and R. Yosei concedes that if the first (original KG) dies, [the replacement] returns to his service. [Objection:] Obvious! [Resolution:] Lest you say he would become a 'tzarah mi-chayim' [a status attaching during the other's lifetime] - this teaches us [otherwise].
reviewEvidence.rashiCrossCheck: 12b.learning.json rashiTranslations lines 57-61 (independently glossing the same phrase set) state explicitly: the original disqualification was because of 'kinah' (professional priestly rivalry over who holds the office), and the concern voiced by 'lest you say' is that 'because of rivalry he would remain disqualified even after the first one dies, for if you say he should serve after him, he would become like a rival-wife (tzarah) during the first one's lifetime, like a woman who is a rival to her fellow, of whom it is said: she waits for the other to die - this teaches us that we do not have this concern.' This is the technical halachic concept of tzarat ervah/tzarah mi-chayim: a forbidden-relative status (or here, a disqualification) that attaches to a party during another's lifetime can, under a known body of law, persist permanently even after that other party dies -- the tzarah must 'wait for the other to die' and even then her status is not automatically resolved. The concern raised here is that the replacement KG's disqualification, having attached during the original's lifetime (via the 'rivalry'/kinah mechanism), might likewise persist permanently by analogy to that law, rather than lapsing when the original dies. Rav's ruling ('kama lan') rejects that analogy and holds the disqualification is purely contingent on the original's life and lapses cleanly at death.

defect.currentClaim: The current enrichment uniformly characterizes the tzarah/rival-wife analogy as being about INTERPERSONAL ANIMOSITY OR ENMITY between co-wives ('co-wives in a polygamous household may harbor enmity toward each other', 'the way a tzarah carries lasting enmity', 'legal status and interpersonal dynamics interact', 'unlike co-wife rivalry', 'a tzarah is a permanent co-wife', 'whose animosity persists even after the original dies').
defect.whatSourceActuallySupports: Neither the Gemara text nor Rashi's gloss grounds the tzarah analogy in emotional animosity or enmity between co-wives. Rashi explicitly attributes the ORIGINAL disqualification to 'kinah' (professional priestly rivalry over holding the office, not personal feeling between the two priests, who are not co-wives to begin with), and the tzarah comparison it invokes is the TECHNICAL halachic principle that a disqualified/forbidden status attaching during another party's lifetime can persist permanently after that party's death, as with a tzarah of an ervah who must 'wait for the other to die' and whose permitted status afterward is not automatic. The sugya's point is about the PERSISTENCE MECHANICS of a status tied to another's lifetime, not about feelings of rivalry or enmity carried by the co-wife herself. Framing this as 'enmity'/'animosity' between the replacement and original KG, or between hypothetical co-wives, is a semantic mischaracterization of a legal-status concept as an emotional/interpersonal one, repeated consistently across display, learning, misconceptions, and quiz fields -- exactly the correlated-field failure mode the self-heal protocol warns about (a family of fields repeating the same wrong interpretation so that internal agreement looks like corroboration).

evidence.independentSourceFlowReconstruction: The daf opens mid-sentence, continuing a 13a discussion about conditional divorce formulas by which a High Priest with two wives tries to guarantee he always has exactly one valid wife (so his Yom Kippur service, which requires 'his house' in the singular, is never performed with zero or two houses). Line 1 closes out a prior critique ('...not a get, and he would have served in two houses'). The Gemara then proposes Attempt 1 (lines 2-5): give a single get to one wife, conditioned on her counterpart dying. Rejected: if the counterpart does die, the get becomes retroactively valid and he ends up with no wife at all (קם ליה בלא בית). Attempt 2 (lines 5-10): divorce both wives - one's get conditioned on 'your counterpart does not die,' the other's conditioned on 'you do not enter the synagogue.' Rejected: if the counterpart simply doesn't die and the other wife simply avoids the synagogue, both conditions are satisfied, both gets become valid, and again he is left with no wife. Attempt 3 / the working formula (lines 11-19): wife 1's get is conditioned on 'your counterpart does not die' (unchanged); wife 2's get is instead conditioned on the HUSBAND's own act - his entering the synagogue. Because this condition is under his exclusive control, the two outcomes are truly mutually exclusive, and he can even preempt an impending death of wife 2 by entering the synagogue himself first, retroactively validating her get. Two objections from levirate-marriage law follow, each resolved within the same breath via scriptural amplification: Rav Asi (or Rav Avira) objects that 'his house' (singular) should likewise bar two yevamin from one house from both doing yibum - answered by the doubled word 'yevimto yevimto' amplifying to include them (lines 20-22). Ravina (or Rav Sherevya) objects that an arusah (betrothed-only wife) should then be excluded from yibum since she isn't yet 'in his house' - answered by the word 'ha-chutza' (outward/extra) amplifying to include her (lines 22-23). The daf then pivots to an entirely new topic (line 24 on): a baraita rules that the High Priest who is an onen (acute mourner) performs the Yom Kippur service but may not eat sacrificial food. R. Yehuda adds 'the whole day.' Rava explains this phrase as teaching that it is a mitzva to actively bring the onen KG from his home to serve the entire day, since engagement in the service eases his grief. Abaye challenges: a baraita states in R. Yehuda's own name that an ordinary priest already mid-service who hears a relative has died stops and leaves (R. Yosei disagrees, holding he finishes) - so if R. Yehuda himself holds aninut removes a priest from service, how can Rava read him as mandating that an onen be actively brought in to begin service? The daf ends mid-resolution with the catchword 'lomar,' continuing onto 14a with Rava's revised answer.

perSugya.reasoning: Content (two rejected formulas plus the husband's-own-act solution, the 'left with no wife at all' reasoning for Attempt 1, and the 'both conditions hold at once' reasoning for Attempt 2) matches the source and reflects the prior round's fix correctly. However, two defects remain. (1) display.title says 'After a rejected attempt' (singular), but the sugya's own oneLine/whats/argumentFlow describe TWO distinct rejected attempts before the working formula - an internal inconsistency between the title and the rest of the enrichment. (2) finalRuling states 'This is R. Yehuda's mechanism for the backup-wife arrangement.' This attribution is very likely wrong: in Mishna Yoma 1:1 and its Gemara, the practice of preparing a backup second wife for the High Priest is the position the Sages/anonymous practice follows, and R. Yehuda is on record OBJECTING to it ('אם כן אין לדבר סוף' - 'if so, there is no end to the matter'), not proposing or owning the conditional-divorce mechanism that rescues it. Attributing this entire three-attempt mechanism to 'R. Yehuda' appears to invert his actual role in the sugya. This cannot be fully re-verified from the 13b-only source text supplied in this packet (the backup-wife mishna/dispute is on 13a, not included here), so it is flagged as PLAUSIBLE rather than fully confirmed, with a recommendation to check against the 13a source before certifying.

defects.issue: Says 'a rejected attempt' (singular) while the body of the same sugya (oneLine, whats, argumentFlow) correctly presents TWO distinct rejected formulas before the accepted one.

Attributes the entire backup-wife conditional-divorce mechanism to R. Yehuda ('This is R. Yehuda's mechanism for the backup-wife arrangement'). Per Mishna Yoma 1:1/its Gemara, R. Yehuda is the one who OBJECTS to preparing a backup wife at all ('אין לדבר סוף'); he does not author this mechanism. evidence.independentSourceFlowReconstruction: Lines 1-5 conclude and reject a prior conditional-divorce formula: giving a single wife a get 'on condition your counterpart dies' fails because if she dies, the get becomes retroactively valid and he is left with no wife (and had performed service while in an ambiguous 'house' status). Lines 5-10 reject a second attempt: divorcing both wives, one conditioned on 'your counterpart does not die,' the other on 'you do not enter the synagogue' - this fails because both conditions could hold simultaneously (counterpart doesn't die AND she avoids the synagogue), voiding both marriages and leaving him with none. Lines 11-19 present the working formula: Wife 1's get is conditioned on Wife 2 not dying; Wife 2's get is conditioned on the HUSBAND's own act of entering the synagogue - since he alone controls this act, the two outcomes are truly mutually exclusive. The Gemara notes a residual wrinkle (if Wife 2 appears about to die mid-service there's a two-house problem) resolved by letting the husband preemptively enter the synagogue himself, retroactively validating Wife 2's get. Lines 20-21: Rav Asi/Rav Avira objects - if the 'one house' logic restricts gittin this way, by analogy two yevamot from one deceased brother's household should not both be eligible for yibum; resolved via the doubled scriptural phrase 'yevamato yevamato' (an amplification/ribui) that permits it. Lines 22-23: Ravina/Rav Sherevya raises a second, textually distinct objection - that an arusah (betrothed-only wife) should be excluded from yibum; resolved via the separate word 'hachutza' ('to the outside'), a different amplification. Lines 24-29 open an entirely new topic: a baraita teaches the onen (acute-mourner) Kohen Gadol may perform the Yom Kippur service but may not eat sacrificial food; R. Yehuda adds 'kol hayom' ('the whole day'), which Rava reads as a mitzva to actively bring the onen KG from his home to serve; Abaye challenges this by citing a baraita in which R. Yehuda himself rules that a priest who learns of a relative's death mid-service must stop and leave (R. Yosei disagrees) - creating tension with Rava's reading, which the daf leaves Rava revising as it closes.

Yehuda whatsoever in connection with the backup-wife mechanism - the mechanism is correctly attributed only to 'the Gemara'/'husband', with no misattribution to R. Yehuda (whose actual role, per Mishna Yoma 1:1, is objecting to the backup-wife practice generally, not authoring this get mechanism - and indeed he is not mentioned here at all, correctly). The retroactivity subtlety (lines 16-19: preemptively entering the synagogue to retroactively validate Wife 2's get before she might die) is also correctly captured in step-03 and the learning fields. evidence.findings: Hebrew source (vilna lines 20-23): '...גיטא למפרע מתקיף לה רב אסי ואיתימא רב עוירא אלא מעתה שתי יבמות הבאות מבית אחד לא יתייבמו יבמתו יבמתו ריבה מתקיף לה רבינא ואיתימא רב שרביה אלא מעתה ארוסה לא תתייבם החוצה לרבות את הארוסה'. This confirms: (1) the two objectors are correctly Rav Asi/Rav Avira (first, re: two yevamot from one house) and Ravina/Rav Sherevya (second, re: arusah) - argumentFlow speakers are source-faithful. (2) sourceRef line placement (step-01 at vilnaLine 20, step-02 at vilnaLine 22) correctly matches where each objection's 'מתקיף לה' actually begins, and tracks the sefaria-ref boundary in lineMap (13b.4 vs 13b.5). (3) The resolution mechanisms are two textually distinct amplifications: the first objection is answered by the doubled word 'יבמתו יבמתו' (yevamato yevamato) - a ribbuy from repetition - and the second objection is answered by the separate word 'החוצה' (hachutza, 'outside') in the yibum verse. Neither resolution reinterprets or expansively re-reads the word 'בית'/'bayto' itself; 'bayto' does not even appear in the resolving half of either verse quoted here. However, the sugya's title, oneLine, whats, hint, coreTension, coreMove, ahaMoment, and memoryAnchor fields all claim the shared resolving mechanism is that 'bayto' is read restrictively in the KG's Leviticus 16 context but 'read expansively'/'more inclusive' in the Deuteronomy 25 yibum context - this is a factual misstatement of the actual Gemara mechanism found in the source text at lines 22-23. It also directly contradicts the sugya's own takeaway field and the second misconceptions entry, which correctly state 'the resolution does not reinterpret bayto itself; each objection is answered by its own distinct amplification - yevamato yevamato for the first, hachutza for the second - not a single unifying reinterpretation of bayto.' The enrichment is therefore internally self-contradictory: roughly 7 of 11 semantic fields conflate the two objections under one false shared 'bayto expansion' mechanism, while the takeaway/misconceptions fields (correctly) deny that very mechanism. This is exactly the conflation defect flagged by review instruction (c): the resolving mechanisms for the two objections are distinct scriptural derashot on different words, not a single reinterpretation of 'bayto', and most display/learning fields misrepresent this. The s02/s03 split at line 16/17 is a shared-line boundary (mishna's closing clause 'chelek barosh v'notel chelek barosh' trails into line 17 before 'gemara man tana' begins), consistent with the Sefaria lineMap (14a.3 starts at vilnaLine 12, 14a.4 starts at vilnaLine 17) and the content is not omitted - s02's own quizSeeds[1] already quotes that trailing clause. No cross-daf leak found; daf ends cleanly at vilnaLine 47 ('...keday she-yitbol roshei [ezov]'), matching the authoritativeHebrewLines list.
reviewEvidence.dafSummaryVerdict: VERIFIED - currentDafSummary accurately captures the arc (Rava's resolution of the onen/kol-hayom challenge, the mishna's seven-day KG service, the authorship question, and the para aduma paradox) with no boundary or factual errors at the daf-summary level of generality.

yoma-14a-s01.notes: Covers vilnaLine 1-12. Step-01/02/03 accurately render Rava's reading of 'kol hayom' as a decree lest the onen KG eat (vilnaLine 1, 6-10), Rav Adda bar Ahava's challenge from R. Yehuda's backup-wife ruling (vilnaLine 2-6), and Rava's resolution via the YK universal fast removing the eating-risk (vilnaLine 7-10). Step-04 correctly adds the itroda/distraction point and the question of whether the conditionally-divorced backup wife is even a halachic onen (vilnaLine 11-12, ending precisely at the gemara clause before 'mishna' begins on line 12). Misconceptions, quizSeeds, and finalRuling all track the text with no misattribution. No defects found.

yoma-14a-s02.notes: Covers vilnaLine 12-16 (mishna of the seven-day Parhedrin sequestration). The bulk of the enrichment (step-01, misconceptions, quizSeeds[0], finalRuling) is accurate against vilnaLine 13-16 (zeriqat ha-dam, qetoret, hatavat ha-nerot, haqravat ha-rosh ve-ha-regel). DEFECT: quizSeeds[1] is internally incoherent. Its question - 'On days other than Yom Kippur during the seven-day sequestration, must the Kohen Gadol personally perform the daily services?' - describes a time period that does not exist in the mishna. The mishna's structure is two distinct clauses: (1) vilnaLine 13 'kol shivat ha-yamim' (all seven sequestration days) - mandatory personal service, no 'other days' subset within it; and (2) vilnaLine 15 'u-she'ar kol ha-yamim' (all the OTHER days, i.e. the rest of the year outside the seven-day sequestration and outside Yom Kippur) - voluntary service with first-portion priority, confirmed by Rashi ad loc. on vilnaLine 15 ('le-hativ u-le-hakriv et kol qorban she-yirtzeh maqriv ve-ein ha-mishmar yachol le-akev al yado'). The quiz question's premise conflates these two clauses, implying there are optional-service days nested inside the mandatory seven-day period, which contradicts vilnaLine 13's unqualified mandatory language. This is the exact content the task flagged as the replaced field, and the replacement introduced a new conflation rather than fixing the prior defect cleanly. Affected field: quizSeeds[1] (question text only; the answer content itself is factually correct but attached to a mis-framed question).

yoma-14a-s03.notes: Covers vilnaLine 17-47 (para aduma paradox). The flagged correction - visualizableElements[1] now correctly states the toucher (noge'a), not the sprinkling kohen or the sprinkled-upon, becomes impure - IS accurate and consistent with vilnaLine 35-36 ('la-mazeh u-la-mazin alav tahor ve-noge'a bahen tamei u-mazeh tahor'). However, a parallel error of the same kind survives elsewhere in the sugya's prose. DEFECT 1 (step-03): 'The Sages say... it doesn't imply the reverse effect on the pure' is inaccurate. VilnaLine 31-33 shows the Sages DO derive a reverse effect (pure becomes impure) via kal vachomer ('im al ha-tamei tahor, al ha-tahor lo kol shekken') - they merely source it differently than R. Akiva (kal vachomer vs. the extra 'al ha-tamei' phrase, which they instead apply to the receiving-tumah/intent law of vilnaLine 24-27). Stating flatly that the Sages reject 'the reverse effect on the pure' erases the actual hinge of the sugya: both R. Akiva and the Sages agree impurity-by-contact exists, but they disagree on WHO it applies to - R. Akiva says the one sprinkled-upon (nif'al hazaah, vilnaLine 19-20: 'tahor she-naf'la alav hazaah tim'ato') becomes impure, while the Sages confine it to the one who merely touches the water (noge'a, vilnaLine 35-36), leaving the sprinkled-upon and the sprinkler pure. DEFECT 2 (step-01): describing R. Akiva's view as water that 'renders pure handlers impure' uses 'handlers' where the text specifically says sprinkled-upon ('tahor she-naf'la alav hazaah', vilnaLine 19-20), blurring exactly the sprinkled-upon/toucher distinction that DEFECT 1 also blurs and that the whole sugya exists to resolve (this is the same category of error the task asked to check for, just surviving in a different field than the one already fixed). Affected fields: argumentFlow step-01 (word choice 'handlers'), argumentFlow step-03 ('doesn't imply the reverse effect on the pure').

yoma-14a-s01.notes: Spot-checked declaredLineRange 1-12 against vilnaLines 1-12 and Rashi glosses (aninut/Yom Kippur exemption, 'miGarsha' divorce-by-death retroactivity, 'mitrad' = occupied with burial). Content matches raw Hebrew; no new defects found. Boundary with s02 is a clean mid-line-12 split at the mishna's ':' marker ('... מי לא מיטריד: מתני׳ כל') — acceptable overlap, not a defect.

yoma-14a-s02.notes: Fix #1 verified against vilnaLines 13-16. Mishna text: 'כל שבעת הימים הוא זורק את הדם... ושאר כל הימים אם רצה להקריב מקריב שכהן גדול מקריב חלק בראש ונוטל חלק בראש' (lines 13-17). quizSeeds[1] now correctly frames the contrast as: during the seven days, KG performs the listed services as of right (vilnaLine 13-15a); on 'she'ar kol ha-yamim' (all days outside both Yom Kippur and the seven-day sequestration, line 15b-16), performance is optional ('im ratza l'hakriv makriv') but the first-portion privilege remains. This is coherent and accurate — it no longer implies a nonexistent third category of days inside the seven-day period. quizSeeds[0] (naming two of the four listed services) also checks out against line 13-14. No other defects found in display/argumentFlow/finalRuling for this sugya.

yoma-14a-s03.notes:
Fix #2 (step-01) verified: matches vilnaLine 19-22 ('טהור שנפלה עליו הזאה טמאתו' / baraita's 'ועל הטהור טמא דברי ר' עקיבא') and Rashi's gloss on line 21 ('ואם הזה על הטהור נעשה טמא'). Accurate.

Fix #3 (step-03) — INDEPENDENT ASSESSMENT: I partially agree with the prior reviewer's flag, and find the current text still inadequate, though for a more nuanced reason than a flat 'Sages derive a reverse effect' claim. The sugya is NOT resolved at line 33 as the enrichment implies. Reading through to the actual resolution:
  - Lines 30-33 (אבל הכא קל וחומר הוא אם על הטמא טהור על הטהור לא כל שכן) ARE a live challenge in the Gemara's own voice against the Rabbanan's limitation-only reading of 'al hatamei' — arguing that even without the drasha, a reverse effect on the pure should follow by kal vachomer. Rashi's gloss on 'vechachamim omrim' (cited for line 22-24: 'שאין דברי הזאה אמורים אלא בדברים המקבלים טומאה... ואין הזאה הניתזת עליהן קרויה הזיה') covers only the baseline limitation and does NOT address this later kal-vachomer challenge, so Rashi cannot be invoked to settle it one way or the other.
  - R. Akiva's response in his own voice at line 33-34 ('ור' עקיבא היינו דקאמר שלמה אמרתי אחכמה והיא רחוקה ממני') is R. Akiva owning that his position is a hard chok, NOT an answer attributed to the Rabbanan.
  - The Rabbanan's actual answer is at line 35-36: 'ורבנן ההוא למזה ולמזין עליו טהור ונוגע בהן טמא' — the Rabbanan hold that BOTH the sprinkler AND the ones sprinkled upon remain pure; it is only one who TOUCHES the leftover water who becomes impure. This is how the kal-vachomer challenge of lines 30-33 is actually defused: the Rabbanan deny the premise that the sprinkled-upon pure person becomes impure at all, relocating the 'al hatahor tamei' effect onto an unrelated party (the toucher of remaining water), not the Mezukan/sprinkled person.
  - Given this, step-03's conclusion ('doesn't imply the reverse effect on the pure [person sprinkled upon]') is directionally defensible as a characterization of the FINAL Rabbanan position, but the text as written is still a DEFECT because (a) it is sourced only to vilnaLine 24, silently skipping the entire intervening dispute at lines 28-36 that is necessary to understand WHY there's no reverse effect (the kal-vachomer challenge and its resolution via the toucher/sprinkled-upon distinction), and (b) by omitting this, it leaves the false impression that the Sages' position was simple and uncontested, when in fact the Gemara itself raises and must resolve exactly the 'reverse effect' problem the prior reviewer flagged. The argumentFlow has a real coverage gap: it jumps from step-03 (line 24) to step-04 (line 24, mishna illustration) to step-05 (lines 36-44, mazeh/shiur discussion) and never represents lines 28-35 (R. Akiva's own derivation of his view from the extra word 'עליו', the kal-vachomer challenge to the Rabbanan, R. Akiva's 'Shlomo amarti' remark, and the Rabbanan's toucher-vs-sprinkled resolution) as its own step(s). This is a substantive content gap in a load-bearing part of the sugya, not a stylistic nit.
  - Recommend: add a step between current step-03 and step-04 covering vilnaLine 28-35 (R. Akiva derives both reverse effects from the superfluous 'עליו'; Gemara challenges the Rabbanan with a kal vachomer that the reverse effect should follow anyway; Rabbanan resolve this by holding the sprinkled-upon stays pure and only the toucher of leftover water becomes impure), and adjust step-03's text/sourceRefs to not imply this is settled by line 24 alone.
  - finalRuling ('mishna follows Chakhamim not R. Akiva') is fine on its own terms but would benefit from reflecting that the Rabbanan's position on the sprinkled-upon KG being unaffected (pure stays pure) is precisely what resolves the incompatibility with the mishna, rather than only Rav Chisda's step-01 contradiction.
  - All other checked fields (quantities 1-7 days, speaker attributions Rav Chisda/R. Akiva/Chachamim, misconceptions, topicTags, alternateAngles on chukim, declaredLineRange 17-47 fully covering the remainder of the daf with no gap) are accurate and well-formed; the single defect above is the basis for REJECTED.

reviewEvidence.dafSummaryNotes: The summary calls the final dispute a 'three-way dispute between Abba Shaul and the Rabbanan' — that is only two parties (Abba Shaul vs. the Rabbanan/anonymous baraita), not a three-way dispute. Also, because the summary describes the Abba Shaul/Rabbanan disagreement only generically (without stating which side holds which order), it does not itself state the reversal found in s03, but it inherits the ambiguity that the underlying sugya enrichment gets backwards. The earlier parts of the summary (R. Akiva/Abaye sprinkling resolution; Tamid vs. seder yoma man-tana identification) are accurate to the source.

yoma-14b-s01.notes: Content of the enrichment (Abaye's resolution: KG serves all day while pure, sprinkled only toward evening, then immerses and awaits nightfall) is accurate to vilnaLines 1-3 ('ראשי גבעולין ... אביי אמר אפילו תימא ר"ע דעביד עבודה כוליה יומא ולפניא מדו עליה וטביל ועביד הערב השמש'). However, declaredLineRange is startVilnaLine=1, endVilnaLine=1 only. VilnaLine 2 ('ר"ע דעביד עבודה כוליה יומא ולפניא מדו') is mid-sentence continuation of the same Abaye statement begun on line 1 and finished on line 3 — it is not a self-contained unit. Because s02's declaredLineRange starts at 3, vilnaLine 2 falls into an uncovered gap between s01 and s02. This is a genuine line-coverage gap, not just a stylistic nit: every vilnaLine must be covered by exactly one sugya, and line 2 currently is covered by none. The sentence content is already reflected inside s01's own enrichment text, so the fix is to extend s01's declaredLineRange to 1-2 (or 1-3) rather than a content rewrite.

yoma-14b-s02.notes: The substantive content is accurate: it correctly identifies the Tamid-vs-seder-yoma order contradiction (Tamid's mishna text order implies incense-before-lamps; the Yoma lottery mishna lists lamp-cleaning before incense), correctly uses the 'man tana' idiom as 'whose Tannaitic view does this anonymous ruling follow' rather than literal tractate authorship (lineIds yoma-014b-l07/l11/l14 and their paired vilnaLines 7/11/14 are internally consistent and correctly zero-padded), and correctly traces Rav Huna's attribution to R. Shimon ish HaMitzpah for Tamid, its refutation via the baraita showing he departs from Tamid's blood-order, and Rabbi Yochanan's reattribution to seder yoma. The defect is boundary-only: declaredLineRange starts at vilnaLine 3, leaving vilnaLine 2 (part of the same continuous Abaye statement that s01 begins) in an uncovered gap between s01 and s02 (see s01 notes). This must be corrected together with s01 so lines 1-15 are covered with no gap before this sugya can be certified.

yoma-14b-s03.notes: CONFIRMED FACTUAL REVERSAL: the enrichment swaps Abba Shaul's and the Rabbanan's positions on where incense falls relative to lamp-cleaning. The baraita at vilnaLines 25-28 reads: 'לא ייטיב את הנרות ואח"כ יקטיר אלא יקטיר ואחר כך ייטיב' (the anonymous/Rabbanan view: he does NOT tend the lamps and then burn incense; RATHER he burns incense and AFTERWARD tends [the last two lamps] — i.e., five lamps, then incense, then the final two lamps) and 'אבא שאול אומר מטיב ואחר כך מקטיר' (Abba Shaul: he tends [the lamps, all seven, with the Tamid-blood sprinkling as the pause between the two lamp sessions] and ONLY AFTERWARD burns incense — i.e., incense comes LAST, after all lamp-cleaning is finished, not first). Abba Shaul's own proof-text at vilnaLines 28-30 ('בבקר בבקר בהיטיבו את הנרות והדר יקטירנה' — 'morning by morning, when he tends the lamps, and THEN he shall burn it') explicitly has tending the lamps before burning incense, confirming incense-last for Abba Shaul. The bundled relevantRashi for this sugya (vilnaLine 58) says the same thing explicitly: 'Abba Shaul says: he cleans — all of them before the incense, with the daily offering's blood as the pause.' But the currentEnrichment's display.whats, learning fields, argumentFlow step-03, memoryAnchor, visualizableElements sequence, quizSeeds answer, and finalRuling all state the opposite: 'Abba Shaul: incense is burned before all lamp-cleaning... Rabbanan: five lamps first, then incense, then the two remaining lamps.' The Rabbanan side (five-incense-two) happens to be correctly stated, but Abba Shaul's side is reversed (enrichment says incense-first; source and its own cited Rashi say incense-last/after all lamp-cleaning). This is a substantive, source-contradicted error that invalidates every field built on the dispute description and requires a full rewrite of display, learning, argumentFlow step-03, misconceptions, visualizableElements, quizSeeds, and finalRuling for this sugya. The underlying two-stage resolution (five lamps cleaned first, two cleaned later, pause differs by opinion) and the earlier internal-Yoma-contradiction framing (step-01, step-02) are accurate and can be kept.

Abba Shaul's own proof-text at vilnaLines 28-30 ('בבקר בבקר בהיטיבו את הנרות והדר יקטירנה' — 'morning by morning, when he tends the lamps, and THEN he shall burn it') explicitly has tending the lamps before burning incense, confirming incense-last for Abba Shaul. The bundled relevantRashi for this sugya (vilnaLine 58) says the same thing explicitly: 'Abba Shaul says: he cleans — all of them before the incense, with the daily offering's blood as the pause.' But the currentEnrichment's display.whats, learning fields, argumentFlow step-03, memoryAnchor, visualizableElements sequence, quizSeeds answer, and finalRuling all state the opposite: 'Abba Shaul: incense is burned before all lamp-cleaning... Rabbanan: five lamps first, then incense, then the two remaining lamps.' The Rabbanan side (five-incense-two) happens to be correctly stated, but Abba Shaul's side is reversed (enrichment says incense-first; source and its own cited Rashi say incense-last/after all lamp-cleaning). This is a substantive, source-contradicted error that invalidates every field built on the dispute description and requires a full rewrite of display, learning, argumentFlow step-03, misconceptions, visualizableElements, quizSeeds, and finalRuling for this sugya. The underlying two-stage resolution (five lamps cleaned first, two cleaned later, pause differs by opinion) and the earlier internal-Yoma-contradiction framing (step-01, step-02) are accurate and can be kept.

reviewEvidence.findings: Independent source-first review of yoma-15a-s03 (vilna lines 27-47), performed without reading any prior review record's reasoning text, using authoritativeHebrewLines from scripts/semantic_daf_packet.py --second-pass. DEFECT FOUND: the candidate's description of the ORDINARY (baseline) tamid blood-application practice is factually wrong about the number of throws. Lines 27-29 read: תני ליה גופא בא לו לקרן מזרחית צפונית נותן מזרחית צפונית מערבית דרומית נותן מערבית דרומית -- the kohen comes to the NORTHEASTERN corner and applies blood there (one application, reckoned as reaching two walls since it is a corner), THEN separately comes to the SOUTHWESTERN corner and applies blood there (a second, separate application, likewise reckoned as reaching two walls). This is TWO separate diagonal corner-applications (NE, then SW), not a single throw spanning both corners. Only R. Shimon ish HaMitzpah's version (lines 29-32) modifies the SECOND of these two applications, replacing the SW diagonal throw with two separate single-wall throws (west, then south). R. Yochanan's count-based explanation (lines 36-38: one application that is two, olah-style; two applications that are two, chatat-style) only makes sense against a baseline of two diagonal corner-throws for the ordinary practice; it is not a description of R. Shimon's three-throw version against a one-throw ordinary baseline. The candidate's display.whats ('The Tamid mishna's ordinary practice is one diagonal throw covering the NE and SW corners'), learning.coreTension ('The ordinary practice reaches all four altar corners via a single diagonal throw (NE-SW combined, in olah style)'), argumentFlow step-01 text ('he comes to the NE corner and applies blood NE-SW together (one diagonal throw)'), and visualizableElements[0] ('ordinary single diagonal throw (NE-SW)') all state that the ordinary practice uses ONE throw reaching both corners, when the source describes TWO separate corner-throws (NE, then SW). Required correction: these fields must describe the ordinary practice as two separate diagonal corner-applications (at the NE corner, then at the SW corner, each counted as 'one that is two'), and must describe R. Shimon ish HaMitzpah's change as replacing only the second (SW) diagonal throw with two separate single-wall throws (west, then south) -- not as replacing a single ordinary throw with three throws. The remaining fields reviewed (R. Yochanan's hekesh to Numbers 28:15, the rejected doubling proposal at lines 37-39, the rejected height-based division at lines 41-43, the two explained-away precedents at lines 43-46, and the mid-word daf ending at line 47) were independently verified against the source and are accurate; only the ordinary-practice throw-count description is defective, but per the holistic-repair rule the entire affected record needs review and correction together since the miscount propagates through display, learning, argumentFlow, and visualizableElements.
